profile.campus: QTS Phoenix 2 (PHX2), 1200 to 1500 North 40th Street, Phoenix, Arizona
profile.reading:
The building mapped here is one of the five data centres on QTS Phoenix 2, a campus that runs along the west side of North 40th Street between McDowell Road and the Loop 202 Red Mountain Freeway, in the Camelback East village of Phoenix. Maricopa County parcel records resolve exactly which building it is. Assessor parcel 121-01-640, whose boundary contains this record's coordinates, carries the situs address 1500 North 40th Street, Phoenix, Arizona 85008, is classified under the county's data centre property use code, and is owned by QTS Phoenix II DC5 LLC, a single purpose entity whose mailing address is 6601 College Boulevard, Overland Park, Kansas, the head office of QTS itself. The county records the parcel at 18.61 acres, two storeys, and a construction year of 2024. Its deed was recorded in February 2024. An earlier version of this registry entry carried an address on East McDowell Road that reverse geocoding had attached to an apartment complex more than a mile away. That address was wrong and has been replaced with the county's.

QTS, originally Quality Technology Services, was founded in 2003, is headquartered in Overland Park, Kansas, and was taken private by Blackstone in 2021. The five buildings sit on sibling parcels in a single recorded subdivision the county names McDowell Road Data Center Phase 2, all of them inside the Creighton Elementary School District and Phoenix Union High School District 210. The county lists 1200 North 40th Street as DC1 on 12.92 acres with a construction year of 2022, then 1250 as DC2 on 11.48 acres, 1400 as DC3 on 13.06 acres, 1450 as DC4 on 12.53 acres and this parcel as DC5, the last four all dated 2024. Three further parcels in the same subdivision, of 10.44, 3.44 and 1.27 acres, are still carried as vacant. The eight parcels together come to about 83.7 acres, which squares with the roughly 80 acre campus QTS describes.

The land came to this use through a rezoning rather than by sitting idle in an industrial district. In December 2017 the Phoenix Planning Commission heard case Z-62-17-8, the McDowell Road Data Center PUD, which converted 97.85 acres from a patchwork of seven residential and commercial districts, including single family R1-6 covering 25.05 acres, into one planned unit development. Staff described the site as vacant with minimal native vegetation and recommended approval subject to 44 stipulations. Those conditions include a minimum 60 foot building setback from perimeter lot lines, a maximum height of 85 feet reached only beyond 100 feet from the perimeter, and a 100 foot setback for utility equipment yards, loading docks and trash areas from residentially zoned property.

What is not known here matters as much as what is. QTS publishes 210 MW and more of critical campus capacity for the whole five building campus and gives no figure for any single building, so no IT load is recorded for this row. The county carries no building square footage for the parcel. The tenant is not public.

profile.regulatory_note: Siting jurisdiction is the City of Phoenix. The campus land was rezoned to a planned unit development in December 2017 under case Z-62-17-8, the McDowell Road Data Center PUD, covering 97.85 acres with 44 stipulations, a 60 foot minimum perimeter building setback, an 85 foot height maximum with stepbacks, and a 100 foot setback for utility yards, loading docks and trash areas from residential zoning. Phoenix did not define data centres in its zoning ordinance at all until text amendment Z-TA-2-25-Y, which the Mayor and Council adopted on 2 July 2025. profile.address: 120 East Van Buren Street, Phoenix, AZ 85004
profile.reading:
QTS Phoenix 1, which the company codes PHX1, occupies 288,000 square feet at 120 East Van Buren Street in downtown Phoenix, of which 108,000 square feet is raised floor. QTS gives the site 32 MW of utility power capacity. QTS does not own the building: 120 East Van Buren is the Phoenix carrier hotel, owned by Digital Realty, and several operators lease space in it, LightEdge and AIS among them. QTS came by the operation through its acquisition of Carpathia Hosting in 2015.

The distinction QTS draws in its own datasheet is worth keeping. Thirty-two megawatts is the utility service the building can draw, not the IT load its customers run, and the two are not the same number. Directories that list 32 MW as this facility capacity are repeating the utility figure without the qualifier. QTS publishes no IT load for PHX1, so this registry records none.

The electrical plant is described in more detail than most operators offer. There are seventeen generator positions, of which nine hold generators of various sizes and eight are sited and available for more. Bulk diesel storage runs to 10,500 gallons with 80,000 gallons permitted and sited, and there is space set aside for tenants to install their own generators, fuel and UPS. Cooling is two 1,000-ton towers with a third position sited. That pattern, capacity present but deliberately unfilled, is what a carrier-hotel operator builds when it expects tenants to arrive with their own requirements.

For accelerator computing this is a connectivity site rather than a capacity site. A downtown retrofit sharing a building with other operators is not where a large training cluster goes; the value here is that 120 East Van Buren is the best connected building in Phoenix, which matters for inference close to users and for interconnection between networks. QTS own large Phoenix capacity is four miles east on the 40th Street campus, which the company has said will reach beyond 280 MW across five buildings.

This is the northernmost and westernmost of the four QTS buildings that OpenStreetMap contributors have traced on the Fayetteville campus. It sits toward the Tyrone Road end of the site, roughly 1.3 miles from the campus gate address on Highway 54 West, and its mapped outline is the smallest of the four at about 19,100 square metres of ground, near 205,000 square feet, in a long rectangle running about 300 metres north to south and 145 metres across. The campus was permitted under the working name Project Excalibur and reviewed as Development of Regional Impact number 3813 by the Atlanta Regional Commission, opened on 5 January 2023 and closed on 30 January 2023. The applicant of record was National Acquisition Company, LLC. The submitting local government was the City of Fayetteville, which had annexed and rezoned the land in the months before the filing, and the site was described as 615.36 acres falling to 611.66 acres after right of way dedications, lying in land lots 23, 24, 25, 40, 41 and 42 of the 7th District with frontage on Georgia 54 at Floy Farr Parkway, on Tyrone Road and on Veterans Parkway. The programme submitted was 16 buildings, 6.6 million square feet of data centre and 400,000 square feet of office, on a build out year of 2032, at a floor area ratio of 0.26 with 1,420 surface parking spaces.

The review is candid about what the land was. It records the property as entirely wooded and traversed by several streams, finds the proposal not well aligned with regional policy on preserving critical environmental locations and resources, and attaches conditions including the 100 foot vegetative buffer and 150 foot impervious setback for the Whitewater Creek watershed, heat island mitigation across the parking, and coordination with the adjoining Trilith development on road connections. On 28 February 2023 the city planning commission approved the conceptual site plan and schematic elevations. Three accesses were proposed, a right in and right out driveway on State Route 54 at the far south end, a full movement driveway on Tyrone Road nearest this building, and an emergency only connection at Flat Creek Trail.

The programme has since grown at the other end. In December 2025 the council amended the future land use map and rezoned three parcels fronting Veterans Parkway to business park, taking the holding from about 615 acres to about 900. QTS Eastwood, LLC filed a separate Development of Regional Impact for that expansion, named ATL2 East, on 15 January 2026, covering about 313 acres and about 2 million square feet.

reading:
QTS, legally QTS Realty Trust, LLC, was founded in 2003 in Overland Park, Kansas, and went private in a Blackstone acquisition completed August 31, 2021, when Blackstone Infrastructure Partners and its non-traded REIT BREIT paid approximately $10 billion, $78 per share, for the company. It is no longer an independent SEC filer, its prior public CIK, 1577368, now covers only historical pre-acquisition filings.

The company's operator domain, qtsdatacenters.com, now redirects to q.com, whose site lists a US headquarters at 22271 Broderick Drive, Sterling, Virginia, an operations support center in Suwanee, Georgia, and an international office in London. The site describes the portfolio only loosely, as "30+ facilities across North America and Europe," while a secondary Wikipedia summary puts the figure at 28 data center locations across 16 US states and two Netherlands sites, Eemshaven and Groningen, a page whose count and the operator's own site do not fully agree.

The registry here tracks 54 QTS facilities across ten states, Arizona, California, Colorado, Georgia, Illinois, New Jersey, Ohio, Oregon, Texas, and Virginia. As a Blackstone-owned private colocation operator, QTS sits in this registry's colocation and wholesale-landlord category rather than its hyperscaler category, alongside Digital Realty, leasing built capacity to enterprise and cloud tenants rather than running its own end-user compute or cloud service. No megawatt capacity figure or dollar-denominated US construction investment total was located in the sources reviewed this session.
